##### Deeper than four levels

This paragraph carries six sentences so that the paragraph rule reports it, and each one is long enough to lift the document average as well. The engine evaluates the average only once a document reaches ten sentences, so a short fixture would never exercise that rule at all. Every sentence here is written at a deliberate length of roughly twenty five words, which is comfortably above the limit the engine allows. A reader would feel the weight of that immediately, and would have to hold each clause in mind while waiting for the sentence to finish. The padding is honest about itself, because the only job of this paragraph is to make the arithmetic mean climb past the threshold. Nothing in this fixture is intended to read well, and a document that reads this way deserves every finding the engine reports against it.

The closing paragraph adds four more long sentences so that the document comfortably clears the ten sentence sample floor that the average rule requires. Each of these sentences again runs to roughly twenty five words, which keeps the mean above the limit without any single sentence breaching the thirty word cap. That separation matters, because a fixture that tripped both rules with the same sentence could not tell the two rules apart when one of them broke. The average is therefore tripped by the shape of the whole document taken together, rather than by any single individual sentence contained anywhere within it.
